advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the config-aware REMOVE recovery direction-aware and collision-safe so a vendor type shared by blocks/depends_on is disambiguated by inward/outward instead of collapsing to an arbitrary reverse-map winner.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py:177: `    reverse = {v: k for k, v in (link_map or {}).items() if v != SKIP}`
config.local_to_jira_link maps both 'blocks' and 'depends_on' to 'Blocks' (config.py:223-227), so any override that keeps both on one vendor type collapses to a single reverse entry
link_direction.resolve_inbound_link disambiguates a shared 'Blocks' type by inward/outward direction (link_direction.py:42-47) — a capability the str->str `reverse` recovery discards
advisory.finding: The config-aware REMOVE-attribution `reverse` map is direction-unaware and collapses colliding vendor types, so a remapped remote link can be attributed to the wrong rebar relation (or an arbitrary one). The built-in reverse path (resolve_inbound_link via JIRA_LINK_TO_RELATION) disambiguates a shared 'Blocks' link into blocks vs depends_on using inward/outward direction, but `reverse.get(opaque_vendor_type)` uses only vendor-type string equality; when two relations map to the same vendor type (the built-in already maps both blocks and depends_on to 'Blocks', and an operator override to a single custom type preserves that collision) the dict comprehension keeps only the last-inserted relation and ignores link direction.
scenarios: A project overrides its blocking link type to a custom name (e.g. blocks->'Dependency', depends_on->'Dependency'); a managed, locally-absent remote 'Dependency' link is attributed to whichever relation survived the reverse comprehension, ignoring inward vs outward direction, so the REMOVE may target the wrong relation or fire spuriously.

ABSENCE: no test overrides both blocks and depends_on onto one vendor type, nor asserts REMOVE recovery of an inwardIssue vs outwardIssue 'Blocks'-equivalent link
advisory.finding: Tests do not cover the collision/direction case for the config-aware REMOVE recovery: every test either overrides a single symmetric relation (relates_to->'Relationship') or uses SKIP, so the direction-unaware `reverse` collapse (two relations to one vendor type, inward vs outward) is unexercised.
scenarios: A regression in reverse-map direction handling for blocks/depends_on would pass CI unnoticed.

advisory.finding: config.effective_link_map DROPS SKIP-valued relations from its returned map (`return {k: v ... if v != mc.SKIP}`), but no test asserts this: the only effective_link_map tests are default-equals-builtin and the fail-closed MappingConfigError case. A regression that stopped dropping SKIP (leaking a SKIP sentinel to callers who expect only mappable relations) would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a REMOVE-attribution test with a link_map where two relations map to the same vendor type, asserting the intended relation (and gating) is chosen.
evidence: outbound_links.py:177 `reverse = {v: k for k, v in (link_map or {}).items() if v != SKIP}`
config.py:local_to_jira_link maps 'blocks' and 'depends_on' both to 'Blocks' — a native many-to-one
test_link_mapping.py only tests single-relation overrides ({'relates_to':'Relationship'}, {'depends_on':'Dependency'}); no test supplies a link_map with two relations sharing one vendor type
advisory.finding: The config-aware REMOVE reverse map in _diff_link_removals collapses colliding vendor types: `reverse = {v: k for k, v in (link_map or {}).items() if v != SKIP}`. When two relations map to the same vendor link type (the built-in already maps both 'blocks' and 'depends_on' to 'Blocks', and an override can produce the same collision), the inversion keeps only one relation, so a remote link of that type is attributed to whichever relation happens to survive. No test exercises a many-to-one link_map for REMOVE attribution.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests for outbound_differ._effective_link_map_for covering repo_root (not CWD) discovery, SKIP retention, and the None short-circuit, mirroring the _effective_status_map_for tests.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:316-344 defines `_effective_link_map_for` with docstring stating '[mapping] MUST be read from it, never the CWD' and 'Unlike config.effective_link_map (which DROPS SKIP...), this RETAINS SKIP entries'
search_files for 'effective_link_map_for' in tests/ returns '(no matches)'
blocking.finding: The new outbound_differ._effective_link_map_for seam (the UPDATE-path wiring for per-project link maps) has no test at all, whereas its status-axis mirror _effective_status_map_for has dedicated tests including one asserting it reads [mapping] from repo_root, not the process CWD. The untested behaviors carry concrete regression paths: (a) CWD-vs-repo_root discovery (a reconcile pass run from a non-store CWD would resolve the wrong project's overlay — the exact bug the status test guards), (b) SKIP retention (this function RETAINS SKIP entries, unlike config.effective_link_map which drops them — the diff funcs depend on this distinction to suppress REMOVE), and (c) None short-circuit when no project key / no [mapping].
